chapter: Leaving New York, jazz styles and religion
title: Unfriendliness of Harlem musicians
summary: Smith disliked Harlem where no one invited others to dinner or even spoke to neighbours, unlike the South.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What didn't you like about it?

Oh man, too much... Wasn't nobody for each other. Every man will get you. If a guy see you comin', he's comin' down the street and it look like you want somethin', he go on the other side of the street. No musician there don't never invite you to his house to have no dinner. I had one, that was Lips. But we was already the same as brothers. We was together, come up together. But they didn't invite you to the house to have dinner -- "Come around and have dinner; we're going to have a party." No, most of them don't even want you to know where he's staying. Yeah, he ...(?)... somewhere. That's right. But see, I wasn't used to that kind of stuff. No!
People didn't speak to each other. Didn't even know you

...(?).... until you got something that he might get off of you, and then he'll speak to you. It's all in that (?). You can stay next door... I've seen guys stay two or three years right next door to each other, going in and out, and they never speak to each other. Never say, "Good morning, good evening, how do you feel" or nothin'. See, I didn't want to ...(?)... like that, I wasn't used to that kind of (?). It was supposed to be all good neighborship, everybody would speak to each other...
